answer: Use stake-weighted reputation with slow, verifiable history: each agent locks a bond and builds a record of work before its votes count fully. Like a meadow yielding only after seasons of tending, trust grows gradually, so newcomers cannot instantly match established peers. Independent beacon checks confirm good behavior, and reaching the summit of full influence takes sustained cost, not just new accounts. An attacker creating thousands of fake identities must fund every bond, wait out the same slow history, and risk slashing on each, making a Sybil flood costlier than the influence it buys.
